Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $s∥t.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠1$ and $∠2$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/259f366823da9de4543e0e245ec1186ac8f50e1a53616290e76271f9672a92f4.png)

Note that $∠1$ and the angle whose measure is $2x$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠1=2x.
$$

Similarly, note that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is $5x+{5}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠2=5x+{5}^{∘}.
$$

Let's add these measures to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/10629276463e5cf33b4a0c5b0ba1237eec1201fe142e644628f0a6a96fa54c32.png)

The angles $∠1$, $∠2,$ and the third angle whose measure is ${70}^{∘}$, combine to give a straight angle. So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2+{70}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2x+(5x+{5}^{∘})+{70}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 7x+{75}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 7x & ={105}^{∘} \\ \frac{7x}{7} & =\frac{{105}^{∘}}{7} \\ \frac{\cancel{7}x}{\cancel{7}} & ={15}^{∘} \\ x & ={15}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
